headers.//: Vite fingerprints these with a content hash, so a changed file is a changed URL and they can be cached forever.

The vocabulary artifacts: 1.82 MB of coordinates and 1.59 MB of token text. NOT fingerprinted -- Vite copies public/ through with the filenames intact -- so 'immutable' would be a lie the day they are regenerated, and every cached browser would keep a stale map forever. A week is long enough that a returning visitor re-downloads nothing, short enough that a rebuild is not permanent.
